questions.q: What does an Availability Set actually protect VMs against?
options: A failure of the entire datacenter
A shared power/network-switch failure (fault domain) or a planned maintenance reboot (update domain) within one datacenter
A regional network outage affecting all of Azure
Nothing — it is a purely cosmetic grouping
questions.explain: Availability Sets spread VMs across fault domains (shared power/switch) and update domains (maintenance reboot groups) inside a single datacenter.

questions.q: What is a fault domain within an Availability Set?
options: A group of VMs that share a common power source and network switch
A separate Azure region
A group of VMs that are always rebooted together during maintenance
A billing boundary with no hardware meaning
questions.explain: A fault domain groups VMs sharing a power source and network switch, so one hardware failure doesn't take out every VM in the set at once.

questions.q: How does an Availability Zone differ from an Availability Set for VM placement?
options: They are identical mechanisms with different names
An Availability Zone spans physically separate datacenters within a region, while an Availability Set keeps all VMs inside one datacenter
An Availability Set spans multiple regions, while a Zone stays inside one datacenter
Availability Zones only apply to storage, never to VMs
questions.explain: Availability Zones are physically separate datacenters within the same region, giving VMs protection against a full datacenter failure that an Availability Set cannot provide.

questions.q: Can a single VM be placed in both an Availability Set and an Availability Zone at the same time?
options: Yes, always combine them for maximum protection
No — they are mutually exclusive placement mechanisms for a given VM
Only in the East US region
Only for Windows VMs, never Linux
questions.explain: A VM uses one placement mechanism or the other, never both at once.

questions.q: In a zone-enabled region, which option does current Azure guidance generally favor for a new production deployment, and why?
options: Availability Sets, because they are newer
Availability Zones, because they protect against a larger failure (a whole datacenter) for the same basic cost model
Neither — resilience mechanisms don't matter for VMs
Availability Sets, because Zones are deprecated
questions.explain: Availability Zones protect against a bigger class of failure than Availability Sets at a similar cost, making them the modern default where a region supports them.
